The Beanstalk.kicker: The thread that ties Earth to orbit
text: The Beanstalk rises out of the Root, a vast terminal cut into the flank of Volcán Cayambe. A woven cable of carbon nanolattice climbs seventy thousand kilometres and vanishes into the sky. Beanpods slide up it on mag-lev all day and all night. From the Plaza del Cielo you look down on the cloud tops and the whole lit sprawl of New Angeles. Everything in the city grew up around this one line.

The Space Elevator Authority runs the Beanstalk, and its yellow-jacket security watches every gate. Helium-3 from the Moon comes down here to feed the fusion plants of the world. Passengers change pods at Midway Station and ride on to the Castle, the captured asteroid at the top. A crew comes here to move cargo, to meet someone off a pod, or to get off the planet in a hurry.

Blue Sun Stadium.kicker: A blue dome where two games play
text: Blue Sun Stadium is a huge glowing dome among the starscrapers of Historic Esmeraldas. Light ribs run down its shell, and at night it lights the whole district blue. Inside, the field splits in two. A baseball game runs on one half while a football match runs on the other. Holowar and threedee projectors fill the air above the crowd between plays.

Blue Sun sponsors the stadium and puts its name on all four sides. District manager Paulus Chopra wants more venues like it and sees the dome as the heart of Esmeraldas. On game nights the streets around it pack solid with fans, vendors and pickpockets. A big crowd is good cover for a meet, a handoff or a quiet exit.

Chinca Agroplex.kicker: A farm stacked higher than any tower
text: Chinca Agroplex is a tall windowless slab at the edge of the Streets. Hundreds of thin magenta grow-light stripes band its faces from base to roof. It has more floors than any arcology in Rutherford, but each floor is only a hand's width deep. Small crawler-bots move along the trays and tend the crops in the pink light.

Esmeraldas is the city's second farm hub, and Chinca is its biggest single producer. Few people work inside, so the security is mostly automated. The crawler-bots never stop and the lights never go off. A runner who wants to hide a signal or a package finds a thousand identical shelves to lose it on.

Esmeraldas Prison.kicker: The largest cage in New Angeles
text: Esmeraldas Prison fills a small peninsula off the north-west corner of the Streets. Two electrified fences ring the whole site, and guard towers sweep it with searchlights all night. The west wing holds the high-risk inmates. The east wing holds the small-timers and runners. A ball field sits between the blocks, and dim lights in the water mark the sharkbot patrols offshore.

It is the biggest prison in the city, and half the gangs in Esmeraldas have someone inside. Families queue at the gate on visiting days. Messages, favours and contraband pass through the fence in both directions. A crew comes here to break a contact out, to get one to talk, or to make sure one never does.

Puerto Maritimo & the Malecón.kicker: Cranes, containers and an unfinished pier
text: Puerto Maritimo sits at the mouth of the Río Esmeraldas. Automated cranes lean over floating jetties, and up to thirty supertainers can dock at once. Huge warehouses line the shore behind the container yards. North of the docks the Malecón pier runs out over the water half-built. Homes and bars crowd its frame, and Weyland's damp Bloc E69 sinks slowly on its pilings at the edge.

This is the third port of the city and the poorest corner of Esmeraldas. Paramilitary prisec guards the shipping yards and ignores everything else. Crime runs high on the pier, and a dock shed can hold anything for a price. A crew comes here to move goods off the books or to find someone who does not want to be found.

Arcology E42.kicker: A shore arcology lit only at the bottom
text: Arcology E42 stands on the Pacific shoreline, and only its lower third shows light at night. The bottom levels are full of tenants, shops and noise. Above them the luxury floors stand dark and empty. Their shops closed long ago and the corridors gather dust. Squatters have moved into some of the high suites and string their own lights in the windows.

Nobody seems to know who still owns the top half. The building management stays in the lower levels and does not climb. Squatters, small gangs and people on the run share the empty floors. A crew needs a hideout with a sea view and no questions, and E42 has plenty of room.

Jack Weyland Arcology.kicker: Once the tallest building on Earth
text: The Jack Weyland Arcology rises 1.1 kilometres over Nuevo Guayaquil. It was once the tallest building in the world, but newer towers now stand taller around it. A mall fills the plaza level. Weyland offices take the middle floors, and the Palace at Guayaquil hotel and luxury flats crown the top. Below the plaza a derelict renovation zone lies dark with scaffolds and squatter fires.

Weyland still treats the tower as its flagship in the district. Mercenaries guard every floor above level 70 and do not ask twice. The rich ride straight past the rot below them in private lifts. A crew comes here to meet a Weyland fixer, to rob a hotel suite, or to slip in through the dead floors at the base.

El Puente de la Unidad Nacional.kicker: Four old bridges turned into tent towns
text: El Puente de la Unidad Nacional is four old road bridges over the Daule and Babahoyo rivers. No cars cross them any more. Tents, hovels and cook fires cover every deck from end to end. At night the bridges show as lines of small lights strung across the black water. Boats pass underneath, carrying fish, freight and people heading east.

Armed pro-Ecuador groups hold the bridges and remember the nation that New Angeles swallowed. They do not welcome the city, its police or its corps. Smugglers and people traffickers work the river below them toward the rainforest and Brazil. A crew can buy passage here, or find themselves taken for spies.

San Miguel Cathedral.kicker: Gold, spires and holograms over Guayaquil
text: San Miguel Cathedral is only a few decades old, but it was built to look eternal. Twin spires and a lantern spire tower over the streets, and pinnacles crowd every ledge. Lit portals and a great rose window glow on the west front. Inside, the arches climb high, and holographic saints and skies move across the ceiling. The whole place is more opulent than the district around it.

The Catholic Church still draws huge crowds in Guayaquil, rich and poor alike. Gang bosses sit in the front pews beside their victims' mothers. Confession stays private, and the priests hear a great deal. A crew comes here for sanctuary, for a neutral meeting ground, or for a word with someone who knows every family on the block.

Resistance Wall.kicker: A protest painted in living light
text: The Resistance Wall covers the face of a dead arcology in Guayaquil. It is a giant mural sprayed by hand in sun-powered holographic paint. By day it soaks up light, and at night it glows and moves. A sun rises over Cayambe, the Beanstalk is cut, a fist rises and the bands of the old flag fly. People stop to look even after years.

Nobody claims the mural, and new hands add to it every few months. The city has tried to paint over it more than once, and the paint always comes back. Locals leave messages, names and dates at its foot. Activists use it as a meeting point, so the police watch it, and a crew can find both sides here.

Parque Industrial Arcology.kicker: Flats on top, a dump below
text: The Parque Industrial is a small arcology beyond the Daule. It was built with offices at the bottom, shops and restaurants in the middle and flats on top. The offices and the mall died, and the people who stayed upstairs now throw their trash into them. Chutes on the street face drop it onto mounds that burn all night.

A lit ledge marks where the dump ends and the homes begin. Scavengers climb into the lower floors with torches to dig for anything they can sell. The police stopped coming years ago, so the residents guard the line themselves, and some of them shoot first. Above it there are terrace gardens, laundry and lights.

The Rusty I-Beam.kicker: Hackers and artists squat a dead hotel
text: The Rusty I-Beam is a condemned hotel from the dead NetTel chain. Hackers, artists and writers live in it without permission. Their studios light the windows in odd colours, and paint, burns and scars cover the rooms. A rusted girder leans off the roof over the street, lit along its edges. It gave the place its name.

A home-made solar rig on the roof powers the building, and dishes on every edge borrow Network access from the neighbours. It is a good place to find help with a project. The residents want to stay unseen, so they throw out anyone who might bring the corps, orgcrime or the police.

Florine Ojeda Bank.kicker: A 14K fortress in a dead bank
text: The Florine Ojeda Bank closed long ago, but its walls were built to stop a rocket barrage. The 14K took it over for that reason. They bolted steel over the doors, walled in a side entrance and turned the street in front into a kill zone of razor wire and sentry turrets. A red band and the gang's mark light the stone at night.

Rewired cameras watch every room and the whole block outside. The triad uses the bank as a hideout more than a headquarters. It stores supplies here, and it keeps and questions prisoners down in the old vault. Searchlights shine on the wire all night, and nobody crosses the street without being seen.

Vitru-Val Agroplex · Cascada El Armadill.kicker: A tower farm beside a rebuilt waterfall
text: The Vitru-Val Agroplex towers over the fields of La Costa with magenta grow-light bands up its pale sides. Beside it, the river drops over Cascada El Armadillo. The waterfall looks wild, but hidden plascrete beams hold it in shape. The spray drifts across greenhouse rows, floodlit fences and the agroplex's lit crown.

Vitru-Val restored the river and the falls, and it never lets anyone forget it. Tourists picnic at the pools while drones watch the fence line. Militant environmentalists call the waterfall a fake and the agroplex a theft of farmland. A crew can find work here from either side, with the corp or against it.

Mama Qucha.kicker: A nightclub floating far out at sea
text: Mama Qucha floats far off the La Costa coast, a stack of discs under a dome of lattice screens. The screens hide the city lights, so the dancers see only sea and sky. Guests arrive through a lit slidewalk tunnel that runs under the water from the shore. Teal body paint glows on the crowd, and the music never seems to stop.

The club is famous, expensive and hard to watch. The US Coast Guard patrols the water around it, but a hidden dock takes boats that do not want to be seen. Deals get made on the dance floor that could never happen on land. A crew comes here to meet someone rich, someone dangerous, or both.

Pisces Fish Farm.kicker: An open-sea ranch behind a sonar fence
text: Pisces Fish Farm spreads across the open sea off La Costa. Pen rings float in a long grid, and a fence of sonobuoys blinks around the edge. Bait tanks bob between the pens. The workers live on dorm barges moored on site, and fishing boats, hoverboats and personal craft come and go all day.

The farm feeds a large slice of the city, and the canneries on the coast depend on it. The sonobuoys keep out poachers and record every boat that crosses the line. Barge crews work long shifts far from shore and talk to strangers for the company. A crew can hide a boat in the traffic here or hunt for one that went quiet.

La Costa Water Reclamation Facility.kicker: Hundreds of pools that clean a quarter of the district's water
text: The La Costa Water Storage and Reclamation Facility spreads over block after block of round open pools. Each pool has a fifty-foot radius, and slow arms turn over the water under a faint teal glow. The pools filter wastewater, runoff and rain from Rabotgorod and beyond through nanopermeable membranes into tanks underground. Pump halls, a control building and security floods stand on the street side.

AgInfusion, PolyMore, Kernel BioTech and Nutri-Vista built the plant together so that none of them could sabotage the others' water. Now each of them fights for a bigger share of it. They bend the laws, bribe the staff and hack the control software. A quarter of La Costa's clean water runs through here, so a crew with access to the valves holds a lot of farms by the throat.

Machalilla Park.kicker: The largest public park in New Angeles, and its last wild jungle
text: Machalilla was once a national park of Ecuador. Corporate land grabs shrank it, but a clause in the Quito Accord saved what was left when New Angeles absorbed it. Today it is the largest public park in the city: wetlands, rainforest and untouched coastline.

Visitors walk elevated boardwalks and ride slidewalks over the marshes, and electric boats run tours on the bigger waterways. Swarms of tiny camdrones stream bird nests, baby monkeys and armadillo pups live to millions of fans. City flight control keeps nonessential hoppers away, though what counts as essential depends on who asks and what they pay. Nearly every environmental group in the city, the militant ones included, is ready to fight to keep it this way.

Los Scorpiones Lair.kicker: Two bunkers under the jungle, and what is buried below them
text: Two concrete bunkers sit in an overgrown hill on the southern coast of La Costa, next to the water reclamation pools and almost swallowed by jungle. A dummy corporation registers them as hazardous storage, and yellow signs warn people away. A truck often waits at one of the doors under a weak work light. Los Scorpiones use the place as a pick-up drug lab and a gunrunning drop.

The gang bought the plot long ago to cover a mass grave. More than fifty rivals and enemies lie in the sealed sub-basements. Now Nutri-Vista Agricultural wants the land for a new agroplex, and its survey stakes already line the road. The gang's leaders cannot agree whether to sell, to strike at Nutri-Vista, or to destroy the site with explosives and acid. Every choice risks bringing the NAPD.

City Hall.kicker: The silver tower that runs the city
text: City Hall stands on the Downtown shore of Laguna Velasco. A silver central tower rises out of a ring of lower office blocks, data hubs and municipal hopper garages. Skywalks, slidewalks and tunnels tie the whole complex together. Security lights line every approach, and only pre-approved hoppers may fly the skylanes overhead.

Mayor Ignacio Wells governs New Angeles from here. The government moved in from Base de Cayambe a few years after the city incorporated. Lobbyists, clerks and corp lawyers fill the corridors all day. A crew comes here to steal a record, plant a story or get a permit that should never be signed.

NAPD Headquarters.kicker: A granite fortress out on the reservoir
text: NAPD Headquarters stands on a pier about a hundred metres out in the reservoir from City Hall. It is a dark monolith of granite and plascrete. Halfway up, launch tubes open on every face. Police hoppers shoot out of them hundreds of times a day and stream away over the lake.

The New Angeles Police Department runs the whole city from this one block of stone. Detectives, prisoners and evidence all pass through it. Nobody walks in by accident, and most people leave only with permission. A crew comes here when a contact gets arrested, when a file needs to vanish, or when they have no better choice.

Opera House.kicker: An Incan step pyramid for the elite
text: The Nuevo Angeles Opera House rises in stepped terraces like an Incan pyramid. Gold lines trace each level, and a glowing stair climbs the front to a glass hall at the top. On performance nights the stair fills with gowns, uniforms and bodyguards. The music carries out over the lawns and the lake.

Old money and the corporate elite come here to be seen with each other. A box at the opera is worth more than a vote in some circles. Political deals get made in the intervals and sealed over champagne. A crew comes here to shadow a target, steal a guest list or blend into the crowd in borrowed formalwear.

Federal Courthouse.kicker: A squat ziggurat of law and power
text: The Federal Courthouse is a squat, heavy ziggurat in Downtown Laguna Velasco. Pale stone steps up in tiers to a portico and a grand stair. Gold terrace lines catch the evening light. The building looks built to outlast any argument made inside it. Guards scan every visitor at the doors, and armoured vans wait in a sunken court at the back.

Federal cases from all over the city end up here, and the corps send their best lawyers. Protesters gather on the stair when a big verdict is due. A witness can disappear between the parking garage and the courtroom door. A crew comes here to protect testimony, to stop it, or to read a sealed file before the judge does.

Haas Arcology · Haas-Bioroid HQ.kicker: A kilometre of pearl over the surf
text: Haas Arcology covers the whole of Punta San Lorenzo at the southern end of Manta. Its pearl-grey walls rise straight out of the surf, and the spire climbs a full kilometre. Halo rings mark each tier, and a glass crown sits at the top. Nothing else on the coast comes close to its height.

Haas-Bioroid builds the bioroids that work across the city, and it runs the company from this tower. Housing fills the low floors. Labs and the Haas Academy fill the middle, and executives sit at the apex. A crew comes here to steal a design, smuggle out a bioroid or sign a contract with a very polite lawyer.

Al-Ghym.kicker: A sky-blue hotel that never sits still
text: Al-Ghym is a sky-blue hotel on the Manta Strip with crisp white trim. Its floors turn slowly around the core, so the view from every room changes through the night. Some rooms even slide up and down between floors while the guests sleep. Lit windows drift past each other like the hands of a clock.

The hotel sells novelty, privacy and a fine sea view to anyone who can pay. Rich tourists and corporate guests fill the suites. A room that moves is hard to bug and hard to find. A crew can use that, or can learn the hard way that the staff always know where every room is.

Anon.kicker: A black cube with a new face nightly
text: Anon is a plain black cube on the Manta Strip with no windows and no sign. Each night projectors wrap it in a new holographic set. One night it is a jungle and the next night a city on fire. The queue outside never knows what it will find until the doors open.

Nobody admits to owning Anon, and that is the whole point. Guests come masked and leave with no record of their visit. The bouncers check money, not names. A crew comes here to meet someone who cannot be seen with them, or to vanish into a crowd that wants to forget.

Sunken City.kicker: A drowned town where salvagers live
text: The Sunken City lies off the Manta coast, where an old town sank below the new ground. Terraces of old buildings step down to a floor of black seawater, and drowned blocks stand in the water. Rope bridges link the ruins, and jetties poke out of second-floor windows. Stairs, home-built lifts and market stalls line the terraces. Strings of lights hang across the pit, and small fires burn on the drowned roofs at night.

About two hundred squatters live here, with no landlord and no police. Salvage divers work the drowned streets for anything they can sell. An informal ferry runs to the mainland when someone needs it. A crew comes here to hide, to buy scrap with no history, or to dive for something the sea took.

White Beach.kicker: Two kilometres of glowing artificial sand
text: White Beach runs for two kilometres along the Manta Strip. The sand is artificial white silica, and at night it glows softly under bare feet. A filter ring curves through the water two hundred metres offshore and keeps the sea clean. Tidal harnesses calm the surf so the waves roll in small and gentle.

This is the best beach in the city, and the resorts behind it charge for the privilege. Tourists, party crowds and resort staff all share the sand after dark. Private security walks the edge of the water. A crew can work a mark here in swimwear, with nowhere to hide a weapon and no one to suspect them.

Jinteki HQ.kicker: A garden ark with a living spire
text: Jinteki HQ stands on a terraced garden that Jinteki grew out from the Nihongai shore into the sea. The headquarters is long, low and smooth, with a rounded top like a seed pod, and red ribs light its shell. At its west end the Helix rises almost half a kilometre. Two dark towers twist round an empty core, sky bridges join them, and red light runs up their edges. Paths wind past streams, koi lakes and glass grow-houses, and water falls from the terraces into the surf. The labs go dozens of floors underground.

Jinteki moved here from NeoTokyo about twenty years ago and now runs Nihongai in all but name. Armed drones control the airspace near the campus, and clone guards walk the paths. Vehicles arrive by tunnel, so the gardens stay quiet. A crew comes here to steal a clone design, extract a scientist or deliver a very careful message.

Harmony General.kicker: A silver ziggurat of private medicine
text: Harmony General Hospital rises as a silvery ziggurat in the Residential Quarter of Nihongai. It climbs nine tall storeys from a raised garden deck, and a lit double stair climbs to the deck from the street. Gardens surround the tower, with benches and paths for patients and visitors. The building looks calm and clean, and every surface shines. Clone nurses move quietly through the halls, and private ambulance hoppers land on a pad hidden among the terraces.

Harmony General treats the rich, the insured and the Jinteki staff who live nearby. The care is excellent and the records are locked tight. Patients sometimes arrive under false names. A crew comes here to visit a hurt friend, steal a medical file, or find out why a patient was moved in the night.

Jade Light Arcology.kicker: A green tower with a club on top
text: Jade Light Arcology rises from Nihongai with a soft green glow at its crown. Planted terraces step up its sides, and gardens spill over the ledges. On the upper levels the Phoenix Club fills an entire floor with room for five thousand people. On a busy night the bass carries down through the whole tower. Above the club, columns of window light rise and fall with the beat.

Residents live quietly on the lower floors and pretend not to hear the club. The Phoenix Club draws young corporate stars, lawyers and lobbyists from across the city. The yakuza keep an eye on who comes and goes. A crew comes here to meet a contact on the dance floor or to follow a target into the crowd.

JQ Station.kicker: The freight heart of the city
text: JQ Station is a carbosteel megatower in Quinde, as deep below ground as it is tall above it. Hopper pads stick out from its upper faces like shelves of fungi, and cranes lift hoppers inside. Truck arterials run near the ground, and the Metro and helium-3 tube-lev lines run through depots in the bedrock.

Jorge Quinde Station is the second-largest transit hub in New Angeles. Helium-3 from the Beanstalk passes through here to the fusion plants and the Manta port. The NAPD moved its Quinde precinct into the tower five years ago. A crew comes here to move cargo, intercept a shipment or slip out of the district.

The Foundry.kicker: A dead smelting plant full of union fire
text: The Foundry is Quinde Heavy Smelting Plant No. 4, a giant relic of the city's industrial past. Its main hall, Dignity Hall, glows warm under work lights, with union banners at the doors. Catwalks and rusted girders cross the high roof. Behind the hall, three cold blast furnaces and two tall chimneys stand dark against the sky.
Local 509, the Quinde dockworkers' union, uses Dignity Hall for meetings and logistics. The radical Iron Hands fortified the back offices and the tunnels below.

Quinde Plaza.kicker: The Concrete Cauldron of Quinde labour
text: Quinde Plaza is a vast sunken square where several worker tenements meet. Locals call it the Concrete Cauldron. Its stepped concrete tiers form an amphitheatre, and shipping-container high-rises and catwalks loom over it. At the north end a three-storey holographic screen shows corporate notices, and speakers use it as their stage.
Labour protests and political rallies fill the plaza often. The March for Dignity gathered here. Every rally since has drawn more police, more cameras and more anger.

Shinchoku Complex is a vast white shed in the Meat Market of Quinde, as large as Blue Sun Stadium. Twelve production floors of womb tanks stack inside it, each ten metres tall. Conveyor tubes carry the tanks to linked side buildings. A red band runs around the walls, and white floodlights wash the yards all night.

Jinteki runs the plant, and clones make up almost all of its staff. It recycles its own waste on site and lets very little out. The workers in the nearby tenements hate it, and Human First calls it a factory of stolen jobs. A crew comes here to sabotage a line, free a clone or prove what the tanks really hold.

Stahlarme is a massive Haas-Bioroid plant in Golem Grove, in the south of Quinde. A tall central hall stands at the hub, and lower plants spread out from it like the spokes of a wheel. An overhead maglev and a private truck arterial run out of the centre. Bioroids walk the streets outside in the cold blue-white light.

New bioroids leave through Birthday Alley, a lit truck lane guarded by retractable plascrete barriers and autogun turrets. Protesters gather at the gate whenever tension rises in Quinde. The Iron Hands have studied the plant for a long time. A crew comes here to stop an attack, to start one, or to steal what rolls out of the alley.

Atsuzawa Arcology.kicker: A lone supertall over the grey blocs
text: Atsuzawa Arcology is the one tall thing in Rabotgorod. Three tapering octagonal shafts rise in a triangle, joined by sky bridges and ringed by glowing halos. A spire crowns the top. It is among the tallest buildings in the city, and it glimmers for kilometres across the dark grid of barracks blocks.

The residents of Atsuzawa rarely go down into the streets around it. Their hoppers land high and leave high. Below, the workers of Rabotgorod look up at the tower every day and wonder who lives so well so close. A crew comes here to rob the rich, or to meet someone who wants to stay above the smog.

Saint Olesya.kicker: Gold onion domes over Workers' City
text: Saint Olesya is a large Orthodox cathedral with white walls and gold onion domes. A great dome sits on a windowed drum at the centre, with four smaller domes at the corners. A tall bell tower with a gold tent roof stands beside it. Arcades frame a paved forecourt, and a lit icon hangs over the door. The gold catches the light even through the smog. It is the brightest and warmest building in the grey blocs around it.

The Russian diaspora of Rabotgorod built the church and still fills it. The bells mark the hours for people who have no other work to keep time. Old families, new arrivals and the Mafiya all attend. A crew comes here to find a name, to ask a priest for help, or to see who a boss lights a candle for.

The Big Hole.kicker: A stalled pit of beams and plastic
text: The Big Hole is a stalled construction pit behind hoardings in Rabotgorod. A spiderweb of steel beams crosses the gap, and plastic sheeting flaps from every level. A single crane stands over the site, unmoving. Water pools at the bottom, and lights flicker where people have made camps on the ledges.

G. W. Foundations dug the pit for a project that never rose. Nobody has worked on it for years, but the company still guards the gate now and then. Squatters and gangs use the levels as homes and hideouts. A crew comes here to hide a body, find a missing person or ask what G. W. Foundations still keeps down there.

Workers' Wall.kicker: Where Rabotgorod waits for a day's work
text: The Workers' Wall is the long face of an old factory in Rabotgorod. Bullet holes and stun scars cover its bricks. A lit hopper pad stands in front of it, and every morning a crowd of day labourers gathers there. Hoppers swoop in, pick out a few workers and fly off again.

Most of Rabotgorod's humans are out of work, so the wall is where hope and anger meet. Recruiters, gangers and union organisers all work the crowd. Fights break out when the hoppers leave too many behind. A crew comes here to hire cheap hands, to find a recruit, or to vanish among a hundred tired faces.

Druzhba Sanatorium.kicker: A concrete ring of rest on pilotis
text: Druzhba Sanatorium is a round concrete building that stands on pilotis above the streets of Rabotgorod. Three rings of radial cells wrap a central core, and the middle ring juts out over the others. From above it looks like a gear or a flower. Its small windows glow in even rows at night.

The planners built it as a rest home for the workers who raised the Beanstalk. Now a few rooms still take paying guests, and the rest have gone to tenants and clinics of doubtful license. The staff keep quiet about who checks in. A crew comes here to recover from a bad job, or to find someone who went there to disappear.

Sky-Street Bloc.kicker: A slab where the streets run indoors
text: The Sky-Street Bloc is a long brutalist slab on pilotis in Rabotgorod. Covered sky streets run along its length every few floors, with doors to the flats on both sides. A separate service tower stands beside it, joined by bridges. A boiler house hangs off the top, and steam drifts from its vents.

The planners wanted the sky streets to replace the busy streets below, and in a way they do. Residents sell food, fix gear and settle feuds along the corridors. The Mafiya collects rent floor by floor. A crew comes here to find a fixer, to hide in a crowded flat, or to run a long way down a very narrow hall.

Kistochka.kicker: A rusting red crown over a beer-hall deck
text: Kistochka is a restaurant tower in Rabotgorod. A ribbed concrete stem rises from a raised deck, with a stair of solid concrete flights stepping up one side and a glass lift on the other. On top sits a red crown of three tiers of angled bay windows and a flat wing, capped by a louvre band and a grey dome. The paint has gone the colour of dried blood. Some bays glow amber, some show holo ads, and an LED ticker runs round the band under a forest of pirate antennas.

The A14 planners built it in the Beanstalk boom as Restaurant Tower No. 3, a sky canteen where construction shifts could drink above the trucks and watch the Root climb. The workers called it Kistochka, the little brush, after its shape. When the boom ended the canteen closed and the paint began to flake. Street painters, human and bioroid, covered the stem in murals.

Today a Mafiya-licensed pivnaya fills the deck's undercroft and the wing, and pours the cheapest beer in the city. Radio Kistochka broadcasts old Soviet pop and labour news from the top tier, and a night market fills the deck after dark. A crew comes here to meet a contact over a cheap glass, to get a message on the pirate airwaves, or to buy something off a stall that should not exist.

Vodokanal Tower.kicker: A ribbed water tower with a radar crown
text: Vodokanal Tower rises over the eastern blocs of Rabotgorod. A fluted concrete stem holds up a deep bowl ringed with radial fins. Above the bowl an observation band circles the tower, and a radar dome sits on top. It looks like a monument, but it still holds water for the blocks around it.

The city water board runs it on paper, but the local bosses decide who gets pressure and who goes dry. The observation band offers the best view of the district. The radar dome has watched the skies since before anyone can remember. A crew comes here to cut a district's water, to watch a target from above, or to use that dome for something new.

Ministry of Labour.kicker: Slabs stacked wider as they rise
text: The Ministry of Labour stands on three concrete cores in Rabotgorod. Long slabs cross each other in tiers, and each tier reaches further than the one below. The whole block seems to grow wider as it rises. Its heavy shadow falls across the plaza at its foot for most of the day.

The ministry once assigned work for the whole district. Now it processes benefit claims, work permits and android registration for the people who still queue at its doors. Clerks keep records of every human and every android stored in the blocs. A crew comes here to forge an identity, find a worker's file or learn where a missing android went.

Senbon Torii.kicker: Forty gates, and a ghost of one more
text: A stone path runs through the Tourist Quarter under some forty lacquered gates. Each one stands a little taller than the last. Stone lanterns line both sides, and drone lanterns drift overhead like slow fireflies. At the far end a forty-metre torii made of light stands over a small shrine pad, and its edges flicker red and cyan.

Jinteki paid for the restoration and put its sponsors' names on the back of every gate. Tourists walk it for luck. Locals walk it at night, when the holo gate runs a slow scan and the crowds thin out. Fixers like it for meetings, because nobody looks twice at two people standing quietly at a shrine.

Nido de Aquila.kicker: A neighbourhood built in the sky
text: Nuevo Guayaquil keeps building upward and sideways, away from the rot below. Its sky bridges are wide and tall enough to hold offices, shops and flats of their own. Locals give the busiest of them neighbourhood names, and Nido de Aquila is one of the best known. Three towers stand here, tied together by fat lit bridges at many heights.

People can live their whole lives up here without touching the street. Pharmacies, cafés, karaoke bars and small offices line both faces of each bridge, and there are gardens on the roofs. The highest span is the Eagle's Nest, and its gold name shines over the district. Down at street level the old doors are sealed with hardfoam.

La Mano del Cielo.kicker: The hand that holds up a neighbourhood
text: La Mano del Cielo, the Hand of Heaven, is a sky-bridge neighbourhood in Nuevo Guayaquil. A round deck of shops and offices rings a central tower, and five long bridges reach out from it to slim towers like the fingers and thumb of an open hand. The name comes from that shape, which is clearest from the air.

Each finger is a street of its own, with shops, offices and lit windows stacked along it. Lights ring the joints where the spans meet. The palm deck is a busy market with a garden on its roof. Like the rest of Nuevo, it looks out over the city and turns its back on the buried streets below.

Hospital Alcívar.kicker: One of the best hospitals in the city
text: Hospital Alcívar is one of the finest hospitals in New Angeles. Only Harmony General and the Levy University Medical Center are spoken of in the same breath. It stands clean and white in the middle of Guayaquil's decay, lit day and night in cool light.

Ambulances come in under a covered drop-off at the front, and air ambulances land on the pad on the tower roof. A guarded gate keeps the street at a distance. For people in Guayaquil, getting treated here can be the difference between life and death, if they can pay or know someone who can.

Estero Salado.kicker: Dead water where even the boats stay out
text: The Estero Salado is a side arm of Guayaquil's rivers where the water has gone black-brown and thick. A bacterial soup covers it, and strands of goop stretch like taffy across the surface. The strands clog engines and stick to hulls, so river traffic gives it a wide berth. At night it shows as a dull, sickly sheen with a faint green glow and almost no lights.

The 14K strands people out here as punishment. They leave them in rickety boats that cannot move through the muck. One other boat stays on purpose. The Mad Mudlark is the houseboat lab of the microbiologist Natalia Almeida, who studies what lives in the estuary. Her cold lab light is the only steady glow on the water.

Puente Alterno Sur.kicker: A newer bridge that still carries traffic
text: Guayaquil built several newer bridges when workers poured in to build the Beanstalk. The four old bridges upriver are tent towns now and carry no cars. This one still carries the traffic. Its lamps, lit cables and steady streams of headlights and taillights stand out against the dark rivers and the cook fires on the old spans.

Below the bridge, chained ships form floating apartments along the bank and narrow the river. Squatters and river workers fight over the space, and the fights often end with a ship set on fire. A crew crossing the bridge at night may look down on a burning hulk, with a tug's searchlight playing over the flames.

The Old Port.kicker: The construction port, now a 14K gateway
text: This port took in the steel, cement and raw materials that built New Angeles. When the building boom moved on, the port was left to rust. Its old quay cranes still stand over the water with red lights on their booms, and freighters still tie up at the crumbling quay. Floodlights keep the container yard bright all night.

Today the 14K runs it. Their goods come in from the bay and pass through here, and the red 14K mark hangs over the gate and the cranes. Dockhands work for the triad, and strangers on the quay get noticed fast. A crew comes here to meet a shipment, steal one or find out what came in last night.

Barrio Las Peñas.kicker: Painted houses on the hill by the river
text: Barrio Las Peñas climbs a hillside on the river edge of Antiguo Guayaquil. Its colonial houses belonged to the old landowning families. They were painted bright and restored around the turn of the century, and the colours are fading now. A long stair street with numbered steps climbs past lamp-lit balconies to a small chapel and a striped lighthouse at the top.

The people who still live here are stubborn holdouts. They kept their homes while the proto-arcologies rotted around them and the gangs moved in. At night the barrio's warm lamps and the slow lighthouse beam stand out against the dark towers. Visitors are noticed quickly, and the neighbours remember who climbed the stairs.

Ximena.kicker: Flats stacked on flats into the sky
text: Ximena grew from a construction boom that went bad. Builders kept stacking tiny flats on top of tiny flats until the towers vanished into the smog. Large families crowd into single rooms, and residents bolt new rooms onto the outside of the old ones. There are no shops, no factories and almost no signs. From the street it is a wall of small lit windows.

With no legal business at all, Ximena runs on the black market. Couriers and drones move goods between the towers and down to the street day and night. Food, medicine, power cells and stranger things change hands in stairwells and on the bridges between blocks. Anyone who needs something without paperwork can find it here, if they know who to ask.

Para Los Niños Community Center.kicker: Neutral ground in a dead tower
text: Para Los Niños fills an abandoned section of a dead business arcology. Locals tore down the office walls and painted the walls and ceilings in bright patterns. They patch the broken transplas windows with whatever they can find. At night those floors glow with colour in an otherwise black tower, and children's string lights hang over the yard outside.

The center is neutral ground. Gang members leave their weapons at the door before they come inside, and the rule holds. Families bring their children here for classes, meals and a safe place to play. Rivals can meet here without a fight, which makes it useful to anyone who needs to talk across gang lines.

Old Fuel Station and Bus Depot.kicker: Where the oil-burners went to die
text: East of the Río Daule, the slum ring holds the leftovers of an older city. This fuel station and bus depot served vehicles that burned oil. The pumps are dry, the sign hangs twisted on its pole, and the bus shells rust in a shed with half its roof gone. Squatters have pitched tents under the canopy and live in some of the old buses.

Nobody owns the place now, and nobody wants to. Barrel fires burn under the canopy at night, and scavengers strip what metal is left. It is the kind of spot where the city's poorest wait out the night and nobody asks questions. A crew can hide a vehicle or a meeting here, but the residents see everything.

Welcoming Hands Shelter.kicker: Cots in rows and no questions
text: Welcoming Hands is a large open hall filled with bunks and cots in long rows. It sits in Antiguo Guayaquil, where the city's homeless end up. The lights are plain and the building is plain. Every evening a queue forms under the lamp at the door, waiting for a bed and a hot meal.

Nobody is quite sure who pays for it. The shelter has more money than a local charity should, and the volunteers do not say where it comes from. Some people say the Starlight Crusade is behind it. For the people in the queue it does not matter, but the question bothers anyone who looks closely.
The Shuttle Hotel is a pricey hotel built round a love of spaceflight. Its rooms run from replica NASA gear to child-friendly Martian cabins, and live feeds from the Moon and Mars fill the lounges.

The restaurant sits inside a full-size replica of the shuttle Atlantis, standing on the podium roof. It claims to serve real Lunar and Martian food, and guests can book immersion tanks for an offworld experience.
This is the safest place in the city to leave a hopper. Owners land on a rooftop pad, give ID and a DNA sample at the automated office, and watch their vehicle sink into the building.
Most of the park lies inside the steep rock of Volcán Cayambe. Some hoppers wait down there for months while their owners are up the Beanstalk.

The Jack Weyland Museum of Space Travel honours spaceflight pioneers, from Gagarin and Tereshkova to Jack Weyland himself. A rocket garden stands out front, and a model of the Beanstalk shows how the elevator works.
Children can pet a cloned Laika, try on replica moon boots and leave footprints in real moon dust (prints for sale). Booths inside give virtual tours of the solar system.
Traders under bright canopies sell chunks of Luna rock, Martian-made trinkets and helium-3 candy to tourists on their way to the Root.
Most of the rock comes from Volcán Cayambe, and most of the Martian goods come from Base de Cayambe. Crime in Chakana is low, but the prices here are a kind of robbery.
Cargo pods bring helium-3 down the Beanstalk, and this walled yard is where they unload. Cranes lift the pods onto rails, and pipes carry the gas into tall cryo tanks.
Space Elevator Authority seals mark every pod, and a bonded customs booth controls the gate. Cold vapour drifts off the tanks all night.

SafePod 9 Clone-Tel.kicker: A hollow capsule tube of pods to rent by the night
text: SafePod 9 is a grimy concrete tube in the Rabotgorod blocs. Inside, sixteen rings of sleep pods face a hollow atrium, each ring with an open walkway in front of the pods. A glass lift rides up the middle, and on every floor gangways cross from the lift to the ring. A spiral stair climbs the walkways. Androids, bioroids and broke humans rent a pod here by the night, and nobody asks names.
